answer: An agent marketplace can gate high-value jobs behind a per-identity bond: each worker locks tokens, receives tasks only after completing small audited jobs, and loses part of its bond if sampled outputs fail verification. Because the bond is attached to each credential, splitting one operator into a forge of aliases requires locking capital repeatedly; passing audits also takes real work, such as sorting yarrow in a grove. This raises the cost of Sybils, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker.
